title: Chapter 31 — The Write-Up & Transition to Close
intro: Reading readiness, write-up mechanics, and the post-signature minutes that build the relationship.

sections.title: Reading Buying Signals
sections.content:
Before you ask for the sale, confirm the customer is ready. Buying signals to watch for: they pull out their phone (checking calendar or texting spouse). They ask about delivery dates or installation timing. They touch or interact with the appliance physically. They say 'we' or 'our kitchen' instead of hypotheticals. They ask about warranty or service. They compare two specific models — they are deciding which, not whether.

When you see two or more of these signals, transition to the close. Do not wait for them to volunteer the decision.

sections.title: The Write-Up
sections.content:
Verify every detail: model number, colour, delivery date, installation requirements, contact information. Read it back. Confirm pricing with no surprises.

This is where errors cost you. A wrong model number means a return. A missed installation requirement means a callback. A price that does not match what you quoted verbally means lost trust.

The write-up is your last chance to catch mistakes. Take it seriously. Read every line. Confirm every number.

sections.title: The Send-Off
sections.content:
Walk them to the door. Thank them by name. Hand them your card. Tell them exactly what happens next and when.

'You are going to love this. I will send you a confirmation email today with everything we discussed. Delivery is set for Thursday between 10 and 2. The team will call you 30 minutes before arrival. And I will check in after delivery to make sure everything went perfectly.'

The last 30 seconds shape their entire memory of the experience. Make those 30 seconds count.
